short: A disastrous French offensive that failed to break the German lines, sparking widespread mutinies across the French Army.
full:
Conceived by General Robert Nivelle as a war-winning strike, the Second Battle of the Aisne began on 16 April 1917. Nivelle promised a decisive rupture of the German defenses within forty-eight hours through overwhelming artillery support and rapid infantry assaults. Instead, the French forces encountered a modernized defense-in-depth along the Chemin des Dames ridge, where German machine-gunners emerged from deep dugouts to mow down the advancing waves.

The offensive stalled almost immediately, devolving into a prolonged slaughter that gained minimal ground while inflicting nearly 120,000 French casualties in a matter of days. The profound failure shattered the morale of the French rank and file, leading to widespread mutinies that effectively paralyzed the French Army for months. Nivelle was swiftly dismissed and replaced by Philippe Pétain, who prioritized restoring discipline and improving conditions while shifting to a defensive posture.
